A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UltraMix study. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and Appendices A–G are readable, allowing retained, relocated, and added material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset annotation analyses and DPO experiments across eight models and fourteen benchmarks, including curation ablations and training-efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds RIP-style filtering comparisons, HelpSteer3 experiments, and further filtering ablations.

M1.justification: The Magpie annotation pipeline, reward model, UltraMix filtering thresholds, task augmentation, and deduplication procedure remain unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Appendix E/Figure 23. New comparator and ablation configurations do not revise the proposed recipe.

E1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds training and filtering experiments using single-turn HelpSteer3 preferences. The five original preference corpora and fourteen downstream benchmarks are retained, making this a limited expansion of data coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated RIP-style reward-gap filtering comparator, including RIP-only and RIP+UM-QF in Table 5 and RIP filtering in the HelpSteer3 comparison. The original dataset comparators remain. AIR is discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: New comparisons specify a 75th-percentile reward-gap filter in Table 5 and a 60th-percentile filter for HelpSteer3. Table 6 states that HelpSteer3 training follows Wang et al. (2025), without listing those settings locally. Existing training configurations and benchmark protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's no-preference-filter ablation is retained, while v2 adds preference-only and quality-only controls in Table 20. Tables 21–22 additionally compare filtered and unfiltered versions of every original corpus on both Llama and Qwen, substantially expanding tests of which curation signals contribute.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The additional tables retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark values are retained, but Tables 5–6 and 20–22 add substantial results for new filtering configurations and HelpSteer3. For example, Table 20 reports Llama overall scores of 51.74 for preference-only filtering and 53.29 for quality-only filtering, against the retained full-UltraMix score of 56.04.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.3 adds mathematical formulations of the DPO loss, implicit reward, and Ψ-PO objective, with Bradley–Terry assumptions and connections to preference quality. This extends the theoretical background without introducing a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and central UltraMix contributions remain unchanged. The introduction now explicitly claims that either prompt-quality or preference-reward filtering alone is insufficient, and Section 2 qualifies the claimed comparison gap in terms of controlled training settings.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a mechanism account involving preference probabilities, gradient signal quality, and task weighting. Appendices B.2 and F.4–F.5 develop interpretations favoring coherence over large reward gaps and clarify that preference filtering alone is not the main performance driver. Appendix G's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an access link for annotated single-turn HelpSteer3 and operational thresholds for the new filtering comparisons. Existing hardware, hyperparameter tables, and curation pseudocode are retained. HelpSteer3 training settings are referenced externally rather than enumerated in the PDF.

R1.justification: New Appendix B.2 substantially expands positioning against Ivison et al., AIR, and RIP, distinguishing sample-level post-hoc curation from dataset-level comparisons and new-data construction. HelpSteer3 and Ψ-PO references further extend the empirical and theoretical context.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include light copyediting, a shortened conclusion, acknowledgments, a conference header, and localized appendix restructuring to accommodate the theoretical discussion, related work, and expanded ablations.

P2.justification: New Tables 5–6 and 20–22 provide dedicated displays for competing filters, HelpSteer3, individual-filter controls, and filtered/unfiltered corpus comparisons. This substantially expands the displayed comparison evidence. Existing figures are retained, while several main tables move and appendix tables are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added component controls and per-corpus filtering tests strengthen support for the unchanged UltraMix recipe beyond v1's no-preference-filter ablation, while the related-work comparisons clarify its contribution. The net gain is limited by incomplete HelpSteer3 settings, unclear aggregation of Table 6's Avg scores, and continued absence of uncertainty reporting.
